conventions.convention: The scalar problem is one-dimensional on the full line. Cells are [jh_m,(j+1)h_m), time levels are nτ_m with n starting at zero, and initialization uses cell averages of one fixed initial datum.

Positive numerical flux points right; the update subtracts τ_m/h_m times right flux minus left flux. One shared interface flux enters adjacent updates with opposite signs. Consistency means continuous F with F(a,a)=f(a); no CFL condition is imposed.
On each cell-time slab the state is U_j^{m,n} and the reconstructed flux is the right-face value Q_{j+1/2}^{m,n}; consequently Q_m(x,t)=F(U_m(x,t),U_m(x+h_m,t)) almost everywhere.

Local boundedness extends to every bounded spatial interval times (0,T') with T'<T. Tests may meet t=0, and the weak identity includes the initial boundary term; neither entropy inequalities nor a strong initial trace are part of this definition.
The weak-limit theorem assumes ACω, strong local L1 convergence in the open time cylinder, and bounds uniform in m up to t=0. Compactness and entropy admissibility are not conclusions.
For Burgers flux s²/2, the Godunov flux takes the minimum over [a,b] when a≤b and the maximum over [b,a] when b<a.

load_bearing.statement: Assume ACω. For continuous f, bounded locally integrable initial datum u₀, and continuous F with F(a,a)=f(a), consider the defined conservative schemes with h_m,τ_m→0 and initial cell averages of u₀. If their reconstructions converge strongly in L1_loc(R×(0,T)) to u and are uniformly locally bounded on every I×[0,T'] with I bounded and T'<T, then u is a locally bounded distributional weak solution with initial datum u₀.

Assume ACω. For reconstructions using a continuous consistent numerical flux, if h_m→0, U_m→u strongly in L1_loc(R×(0,T)), and the states have uniform local bounds up to t=0, then u is locally essentially bounded up to the initial face and Q_m→f(u) in L1(I×(0,T')) for every bounded interval I and T'<T.

For the defined conservative update and space-time test averages Φ_j^{m,n}, if N≥1 and the test vanishes for t≥t_{N−1}^m, then the sum of the initial term Σ_j h_m U_j^{m,0}Φ_j^{m,0}, the time term Σ_{n=1}^{N−1}Σ_j h_m U_j^{m,n}(Φ_j^{m,n}−Φ_j^{m,n−1}), and the flux term Σ_{n=0}^{N−1}Σ_j τ_m Q_{j+1/2}^{m,n}(Φ_{j+1}^{m,n}−Φ_j^{m,n}) equals zero.
The map G defined in def-godunov-flux-for-burgers is continuous on R² and satisfies G(a,a)=f_B(a)=a²/2 for every real a.

published_dependencies.used_for: Scalar Cauchy problem, continuous physical flux, and initial-data conventions.
The initial-boundary-term weak formulation and the distinction between its global boundedness requirement and the batch's local formulation.
The exact ACω assumption inherited by translation continuity, flux convergence, and the weak-limit theorem.
Countable additivity in the face-flux lemma's derivation of countable subadditivity.
Measure estimates and the same subadditivity derivation.
Finite measure of bounded measurable rectangles and integrability of bounded cutoffs.
Compactness of closed bounded state intervals and state squares.
Boundedness of continuous physical and numerical fluxes on compact state sets.
Uniform continuity of the numerical flux on the compact state square.
L1 continuity of spatial translations of the compactly supported cutoff, under ACω.
Translation isometry and change of spatial integration domain in the shifted-state convergence estimate.
The area estimate controlling the strip near t=0, with the chosen endpoint conventions.
The stationary Burgers example's speed calculation with jumps defined as right trace minus left trace.
The nonnegative-test entropy inequality and entropy-pair sign convention used to refute admissibility of the expansion-shock limit.

seams_checked.note: The scheme and interpolant retain the supplier's cells, orientation, initialization, and piecewise-constant reconstruction. The convergence theorem's F5 and step 2.1 apply the weak-limit theorem under ACω after obtaining strong local convergence and invariant-range bounds. Entropy inequalities and the initial trace are established separately.

This is a contextual page prerequisite: the diffusion page's listed items do not cite the scalar weak-limit theorem or its reconstructions. Its outward-from-cell convention expresses the same shared-face cancellation as Q_{K,F}+Q_{L,F}=0. No scalar hyperbolic convergence conclusion is transferred to diffusion.
